doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Copenhagen recordings, interests and views on the music
title: Younger generation and respect for elders
summary: McLean is uncomfortable with young people dropping respect for elders and family, citing 'talk to the hand'.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Are you comfortable with the changing of generations and the changing of the guard in music?
I’m not comfortable with the younger generation and the way they’re trying to change up some very basic things that have always been very important in the black

community, and that is respect for your elders and family, the whole idea of keeping family together and all that. I don’t like young people that cast that to the side, kids that are fresh. Man, I got some kid telling his mother, “Aw, talk to the hand,” you know, put the hand up there in somebody’s face. “Talk to the hand.” I’ll break somebody’s hand if some kid tells me to talk to – have you heard that expression yet?
Aw man. Kid’s do it up here. Like if you’re telling a kid something, so-and-so will say, “Aw, just talk to the hand.” Like, in other words, don’t talk to me. They put their hand up like that.
